blocks.md:
When explaining a natural reason like *“I was hungry, so I ate”* or *“It rained, so the ground is wet”*, Korean uses **-아/어서**.

The vowel harmony rule is the same one you know from **-아요/-어요**:
- Stem ends in **ㅏ, ㅗ** → **-아서**
- Other vowels → **-어서**
- **하다** verbs → **해서**

**CRITICAL RULE**: Never conjugate past tense before **-아/어서**!

❌ 어제 비가 **왔어서**...
⭕ 어제 비가 **와서**...

The past tense is already conveyed at the end of the sentence: *어제 비가 와서 집에 **있었어요**.*

items.tip: I was hungry, so I ate food.
It rained, so I stayed home.
I caught a cold, so I went to the hospital.

blocks.q: Which sentence correctly says "I was busy yesterday, so I couldn't go"?
blocks.why: Never put past tense -았/었- before -아/어서: 바빠서 못 갔어요 is correct.

blocks.meaning: I slept late yesterday, so I am tired today.
blocks.why: 자다 + -아서 = 자서. Do not add past tense inside the connector.
Never use past tense before -아/어서: 비가 와서 우산을 샀어요.

blocks.q: I was hungry, so I ate bread.
blocks.hint: 배가 고프다 → 배가 고파서, 빵을 먹다

blocks.md:
**-(으)니까** expresses a reason based on personal judgment, discovery, or when suggesting an action: *“Since / Because...”*

Attachment rule based on batchim:
- Stem has batchim → **-으니까** *(먹다 → 먹으니까)*
- Stem has no batchim → **-니까** *(가다 → 가니까)*

Unlike **-아/어서**, past tense **CAN** be used before **-(으)니까**!

⭕ 밥을 **먹었으니까** 출발합시다. *(Since we ate, let’s depart.)*

items.tip: Since I am busy right now, let’s talk later.
Since the weather is nice, I feel great.
Since we ate, let’s take a walk.

blocks.q: How do you attach -(으)니까 to 없다 (to not have)?
blocks.why: 없다 has a batchim (ㅄ), so it takes -으니까: 없- + -으니까 = 없으니까.

blocks.meaning: Since I am busy now, please call me back later.
blocks.why: With requests like -해 주세요, -(으)니까 must be used.

blocks.q: Put in order: "Since there is no time, let's depart quickly."
Since it is cold today, put on a coat.

title.en: Lesson 3. The Big Rule: Commands & Suggestions

blocks.md:
This is **the most tested grammar rule in beginner Korean**:

When the second clause is a **command** (*-(으)세요*) or a **suggestion** (*-(으)ㅂ시다 / -(으)ㄹ까요?*):

❌ You CANNOT use **-아/어서**!
⭕ You MUST use **-(으)니까**!

head: Meaning
Wrong (-아/어서)
Correct (-(으)니까)
rows: Because it rains, take an umbrella
Because it is hot, let's turn on A/C
Because weather is nice, shall we go?

blocks.md:
**Formal Written Reasons (-기 때문에)**:
In formal speeches or writing, you also see **-기 때문에** (for nouns: **때문에**):

- 비 **때문에** 늦었어요. *(Late because of rain.)*
- 비가 오**기 때문에** 길이 막혀요. *(Traffic is heavy because it rains.)*
Like -아/어서, it is also not used with commands or suggestions.

blocks.why: Suggestions like -갈까요? and commands like -세요 can never follow -아/어서. They require -(으)니까!

blocks.meaning: Since it is hot, please turn on the air conditioner.
blocks.why: Before a command like 켜세요 (please turn on), use the reason ending -(으)니까: 더우니까. -아/어서 (더워서) cannot lead into a command.

blocks.hint: You cannot use -어서 with command -세요! Change 추워서 to 추우니까.
blocks.why: Commands (-세요) cannot follow -아/어서: 날씨가 추우니까 따뜻하게 입으세요.

blocks.q: Build: "Because it is raining, please take an umbrella."
Since it is hot, please turn on the air conditioner.

title.ko: 4강. 실전 대화: 인사말·사과와 이유 묻고 답하기
title.en: Lesson 4. Real-Life Conversation: Greetings, Apologies, and Decisions

blocks.h: Why Social Greetings and Apologies Only Use -아/어서
blocks.md:
In Korean, social conventions strictly require **-아/어서** for greetings, apologies, and thanks:

- **Apologies (죄송해요 / 미안해요):** 늦**어서** 죄송합니다 (Sorry for being late). *Never* 늦으니까 죄송합니다!
- **Thanks (고마워요 / 감사합니다):** 도와주**셔서** 감사합니다 (Thank you for helping). *Never* 도와주시니까!
- **Greetings (반가워요):** 만나**서** 반가워요 (Nice to meet you). *Never* 만나니까 반가워요!

Use **-(으)니까** when you give a reason to suggest an action, make a request, or give a command (e.g., "Since it's raining, let's take an umbrella").

head: Category
Natural Korean (-아/어서)
Unnatural / Incorrect (-(으)니까)
English Meaning
rows: It’s raining, so use an umbrella

blocks.md: Rule of thumb: If you are saying **thank you**, **sorry**, or **pleased to meet you**, always reach for **-아/어서** without hesitation!

items.tip: I am truly sorry for being late to the appointment. (-어서 for apology)
Thank you sincerely for helping me. (-어서 for thanks)
Since the roads are blocked right now, let’s take the subway. (-(으)니까 before suggestion)

blocks.q: How do you politely apologize for being late: “I am sorry for being late”?
Which sentence naturally thanks someone for a gift?
blocks.why: Expressions of gratitude always take -아/어서: 주다 + -어서 → **줘서 고마워요**.

blocks.q: Match each context with the appropriate conversational phrase.

blocks.meaning: Since the weather is nice today, let's go hang out at the park.
blocks.why: Before a suggestion or invitation (놀러 가요), you must use -(으)니까, never -아/어서.

blocks.q: Conjugate 도와주다 (to help me) into the thanking phrase: 「저를 ___ 고마워요.」
blocks.why: Thanking expressions require -아/어서: 돕다 changes to 도와- + -줘서 → **도와줘서**.

blocks.say: 선생님, 친절하게 가르쳐 주셔서 진심으로 감사합니다.
blocks.rom: seon-saeng-nim, chin-jeol-ha-ge ga-reu-chyeo ju-syeo-seo jin-sim-eu-ro gam-sa-ham-ni-da
blocks.q: Say it aloud politely thanking a teacher.
